_comment: Tunable shared-infrastructure denylists for tools/kb/noise_filters.py. GENERIC public knowledge only (managed-DNS providers, parking services, registrar/privacy-proxy contacts, CDN/SaaS apexes) — NEVER case data, per repo CLAUDE.md RULE 1. This file is DATA: analysts edit it directly, no code change and no redeploy. noise_filters.py holds only the matching LOGIC. Entries are a starter set, not exhaustive — extend as you meet new providers.

managed_dns_suffixes._comment: Managed/registrar DNS whose nameservers are shared by millions of unrelated domains. A `uses_nameserver` edge to one of these must NOT create a same-operator cluster. Dotted entries match as exact-or-parent domain; bare labels (e.g. 'awsdns') match only as a whole dot/dash-delimited label, so an operator's own NS that merely CONTAINS a provider string is not wrongly dropped.

generic_nameserver_labels._comment: Nameserver HOST LABELS that carry no identity — the leading label of an NS hostname when it is merely a sequence number or the word 'nameserver'. Used for DISPLAY, not for clustering: on a managed provider the account-assigned label pair IS the discriminating detail (two domains on hope+rick.ns.cloudflare.com sit in the same Cloudflare account, while the apex 'cloudflare.com' they share is true of millions), so the Domain Summary shows the labels instead of collapsing to the apex. A label listed here is suppressed because 'ns1/ns2' distinguishes nothing, and the apex is then shown instead. Matched EXACTLY against the lowercased first label. Adding a label here only makes a table cell shorter — it can never drop a clustering edge, which is decided by managed_dns_suffixes.

parking_favicon_mmh3._comment: Favicon mmh3 (Shodan/FOFA) hashes of parking / for-sale / marketplace pages. Sharing one clusters PARKED domains, not an operator. 0 = empty/missing favicon. NOTE: a host that soft-200s every path (Hostinger returns its parking HTML for /favicon.ico, content-type text/html) makes the 'favicon' hash a hash of the PAGE — so one value here can stand for millions of domains. Verify a candidate by reversing it: a hit count in the thousands+ means it belongs in this list.

noise_tracker_ids._comment: Analytics / tag-manager IDs that belong to a PLATFORM, TEMPLATE or AGENCY rather than to the site owner, so they must never become a same-owner clustering hub. Two kinds, both observed: (a) a host injects its own ID into its parking/default/error pages, so every tenant carries it; (b) a site-builder TEMPLATE ships with the template author's container in the custom-code slot, so every buyer's site carries it — note this one still sits in the OWNER's editable slot, so 'the owner pasted it' does NOT prove it is theirs. A shared analytics ID is normally strong same-owner evidence, which is exactly why a wrong entry here is costly in both directions. VERIFY BEFORE ADDING: reverse the id and check the hits are unrelated businesses (different sectors/countries), then fetch two of them directly and confirm they serve the same id. The platform's own domains showing up in the reverse is the giveaway. Matched EXACTLY against the tracker value. A site's OWN second tracker stays clusterable — a site commonly carries a shared template container and its own private measurement id side by side, and only the shared one belongs here.

platform_default_favicon_mmh3._comment: Favicon mmh3 hashes shipped as the DEFAULT icon of a hosted platform / funnel builder / CMS, carried by every tenant that never uploaded its own. Same treatment as parking_favicon_mmh3 (recorded as a fact, never a clustering hub) but a distinct group because the meaning differs: a parking favicon says 'this domain is unused', a platform default says 'this tenant did not customise'. Both are read by is_parking_favicon(). Watch for degenerate icons — a default that is only a few dozen bytes cannot carry enough entropy to identify anyone. Verify by reversing: thousands of unrelated tenants means it belongs here.

social_handle_noise._comment: Endings that mark a scraped social 'handle' as not being an account at all. Two kinds: a STATIC ASSET on a social host (github's octocat.png, a share icon — the host matches the platform list but the link declares no account), and an UNSUBSTITUTED TEMPLATE PLACEHOLDER shipped by a bundle ('{u}', '${name}', '%s') which every site built from that library appears to share. Matched against the final path segment, lowercased. Mirrors WebPivot/references/generic_labels.json -> social_asset_extensions, which stops the same values at extraction time; this copy exists because the ingest also reads raw files collected before that filter and must not trust them.

bulk_registrant_max_domains._comment: Above this many domains under one registrant contact (email / name / phone), treat the contact as a SHARED REGISTRATION SERVICE — a reseller, hosting/IT agency, corporate-services firm or an individual holding a resale portfolio — and refuse to link its domains to each other. Such a contact is a fact about who filed the paperwork, not about who runs the sites: the domains typically share nothing else at all, which is the tell (a real operator estate shares favicons, trackers or templates too). This is the ONE number for that judgement and BOTH ingest paths must read it — ingest_reverse_whois.py's --max-domains default and ingest_webpivot.py's reverse-WHOIS fan-out — because they previously disagreed (200 vs 500) and a registrant fell between them. Keep it well under reverse_search_edge_cap: a registrant contact is a far weaker hub than a technical artifact, so it warrants a tighter bound. Raise it only for a genuinely large single-owner estate you have corroborated with a second, independent artifact class.

reverse_search_edge_cap._comment: Maximum number of hits a reverse search (FOFA / urlscan icon-hash, tracker or body query) may return before the ingest refuses to turn that result into `domain -> indicator` edges. This is the BASE-RATE CONTROL on cluster building, and it is the single most important number in this file: without it one collection of a hosted-platform default favicon writes a thousand edges and that indicator becomes the largest 'cluster' in the knowledge base. An artifact carried by more hosts than this is shared infrastructure by definition and cannot single out an operator, whether or not anyone has denylisted its specific value — so this catches the long tail the denylists above never will. The seed's own artifact is still recorded; only the fan-out to reverse-search hits is suppressed. Mirrors WebPivot/references/reporting_thresholds.json -> saturation_ceilings, which applies the same judgement when WORDING an assessment; keep the two consistent. Lower it if junk clusters still appear; raise it only for a genuinely large operator estate you have corroborated another way.

comment_boilerplate._comment: Substrings marking an HTML comment as builder/plugin/snippet boilerplate rather than an operator tell. A shared comment is real same-kit evidence, but only when the comment is DISTINCTIVE — the Google Analytics and Tag Manager snippets, Open Graph section markers and site-builder slot markers ship identically on millions of sites and fuse unrelated domains into one 'template' cluster. Matched as a lowercase substring against the whitespace-collapsed comment, so keep entries specific enough not to swallow an operator's own wording. Comments shorter than min_length are dropped outright: a comment of '$' or 'Twitter' carries no signal at all.

comment_min_length._comment: Minimum collapsed length before an HTML comment may seed a same_comment edge. Below this a comment is a section marker or a build artifact, never an operator fingerprint.

dom_skeleton_min_tags._comment: Minimum number of HTML tags a page must have before its tag-skeleton hash may seed a same_template edge. A page with no tags hashes to sha1('') and every empty, blocked, JSON or plain-text response in the knowledge base collapses onto that one value as if they shared a template — the failure this threshold exists to stop. A handful of tags (html/head/body/title) is likewise universal and identifies nobody.

parking_host_substrings._comment: Host substrings marking parking / sinkhole / marketplace infra (not operator infra). Matched as a plain substring — keep entries distinctive enough not to hit real domains.

role_email_localparts._comment: Email local-parts that mark a registrar/registry ROLE mailbox rather than a registrant. Matched exactly, plus any local-part starting with 'abuse' and any address whose domain's FIRST LABEL is 'abuse' (abuse.<registrar>.com). Keep these role words exact — 'legal' as a substring would eat a legitimate registrant such as legalservices@…

registrar_email_domains._comment: Email domains belonging to registrars and privacy proxies. An address here is the provider's contact, shared by every domain they front — never the registrant.

privacy_email_tokens._comment: Substrings marking a WHOIS privacy-proxy email domain, whatever the provider — catches the long tail without enumerating every proxy. Also reused to detect a privacy-proxy registrant ORG string. Keep conservative so real consumer mail domains pass.

privacy_proxy_phones._comment: Registrant phones published by a privacy/proxy provider across EVERY domain it fronts, so a `registered_by -> phone` edge would merge thousands of unrelated domains. Digits only, no '+' or separators — the matcher normalises input. ONLY add numbers you have actually OBSERVED published as a named privacy org's contact block, never guesses. Note the general rule in noise_filters.is_noise_phone covers unlisted providers when you pass the record's registrant email/org. Also REGISTRAR contact phones that a ccTLD WHOIS (e.g. .vn via Chongluadao) returns in the registrant slot — 84435501630 is Tenten/GMO-Z.com RUNSYSTEM's switchboard, stamped on thousands of domains.

placeholder_phones._comment: Filler typed to satisfy a required WHOIS field. Exact matches only — a general 'sequential digits' test would eat real numbers.

phone_length._comment: A phone shorter than min or longer than max digits cannot be a real MSISDN (E.164 caps at 15).

shared_infra_apexes._comment: Registrable apexes that are shared infrastructure — CDN, analytics, social, SaaS, registrar, parking, marketplace. Matched exact-or-parent, so `foo.cloudfront.net` is caught by `cloudfront.net`. Never an operator lead.

saas_tenant_suffixes._comment: Platforms where the APEX is infrastructure but `<tenant>.<suffix>` is a REAL, separately-owned site — scam operators host on these constantly. Matched EXACTLY (bare apex = noise, tenant = keep), so suffix-matching never silently drops a live target.

shared_hosting_max_cohosts._comment: Above this many distinct registrable apexes answering on one IP, the IP is SHARED / bulk hosting (or a CDN edge) and a `hosted_on` edge to it is co-tenancy, not ownership: ingest records it as a fact, the cluster partition ignores it, and the frontier holds its co-tenants back as a lead. This is the ONE number for that judgement — tools/case_state.py MAX_IP_COHOSTS reads it — so the frontier and the KB cannot disagree about which IP is a landlord.

social_reserved_paths._comment: Per-network FIRST path segments on a social host that are the platform's own routes, never an account: sharing/intent endpoints, media/embed players, login/help/legal pages, repo-level words. A scraped social link whose first segment is listed here is content or a widget, not a handle, and is dropped (`social_handle()` returns None). `*` applies to every network. Extend when a network's boilerplate shows up as a shared 'contact' in shared.txt.

social_second_segment_networks._comment: Networks whose account sits in the SECOND path segment behind a routing word (youtube.com/c/<name>, /user/<name>, /channel/<id>; facebook.com/pages/<name>; t.me/s/<name>; zalo.me/g/<group>). The router word is listed per network; anything else keeps the first segment (or the @handle form).

social_noise_accounts._comment: Per-network ACCOUNTS that are library / vendor / platform credits every site built from a common stack links to (a core-js polyfill banner, a jQuery footer, a theme author), never the site operator's own contact. Matched case-insensitively against the account social_handle() resolved. Extend when a credit shows up as a shared 'contact' in shared.txt binding unrelated sites.

social_platform_apexes._comment: A scraped social 'handle' whose value is the PLATFORM'S OWN apex carries no account: virtually every site on the web links to facebook.com or t.me, so clustering two domains on one asserts they share an operator because they both have a Facebook link. Values here are matched as a whole host (optionally with a leading www.), never as a substring, so a real account under the platform (t.me/some_channel) is unaffected. ADD a platform when you see its bare apex bridging unrelated cases.
